messages:
jin: Heads-up — I’m seeing a ~15% tail-latency regression on paged-attn after landing the pager allocation-hint change this morning. Repro on a small canary (dedicated pool). p99 went from ~70ms to ~82ms. Trace attached.

tara: Hmm. which hint did we flip? slab_prefer -> hybrid?

jin: we set KV_PAGER_ALLOC_HINT=adaptive (was slab_prefer). The idea was to reduce fragmentation, but maybe it increases page walks.

alex: Can you paste the microtrace? Also any kernel fallback events (flashattention -> fallback kernel)?

jin: paste below. note the spike aligns with a lot of PageTable walk syscalls and increased memcpy time around token 1024.
```
[2026-03-12T10:14:23Z] request id=abc123 model=redwood/llama-93b variant=quantized
--- profile
kv_pager.alloc_hint=adaptive
kv_pager.evictions=42
kv_pager.page_load_ms=18.3
kernel=flashattn_v2 (selected)
kernel.fallbacks=3
latency.p99=82.1ms
```

mike: adaptive tries to balance slab vs direct; maybe it fragments differently under the paged blocktable layout. Did you run the allocator frag tool?

jin: ran quick compaction trace: free runs increased but free contiguous block sizes decreased. Attaching short command:
```
./tools/kv-frag-check --pool=/dev/gpu0 --dump=frag.json
jq '.free_runs | length, .largest_free' frag.json
```

anya: Could also be interaction with batching heuristics — larger batches amplify cache misses in the KV pager. What was QPS and batch size on the canary?

jin: qps ~50, batch target=8 (autoscaler pegged). When load drops we see p99 back to ~73ms. So likely a contention + allocation hotspot.

perf-bot: Quick synthetic run attached: fused-attn vs flashattn variants on the same model + paged KV baseline. Numbers (tokens/s): fused=410, flashv2=430, flashv2+paged=395.

tara: interesting — flashv2 degraded more with paged. Could be kernel's memory access pattern not friendly to fragmented pages. We should try forcing kernel selection to fused for the canary and see if regression goes away.

alex: Repro steps we should do:
1) deploy with KV_PAGER_ALLOC_HINT=slab_prefer (old) and collect alloc map + perf.
2) deploy with adaptive (current) + forced kernel fused via KERNEL_PREFERENCE=fused.
3) run the frag tool and perf record: `perf record -F 99 -g -- ./serve --model ... --load 50qps --batch 8`

mike: I can spin a tiny canary and run both. If fused fixes it, we can either change the alloc hint back or make kernel selection aware of pager fragmentation: prefer fused when avg free-run-size < threshold.

anya: We should also add telemetry: expose kv_pager.largest_free_run and kernel_choice to Console SLO dashboard. Alert if largest_free_run < 64k and p99 > baseline *1.1.

jin: Agreed. I’ll add a quick patch to emit those metrics (kv_pager.largest_free_run, kv_pager.alloc_hint).

tara: For long term: consider hybrid allocation that pins hot KV pages contiguous in a reserved slab region to avoid page walks for recent prompts. Might be heavy but worth prototyping.

mike: One more datapoint: when I simulated heavy prompt prefix reuse (lots of KV cache hits), the regression disappears. So the problem is primarily page churn during mixed-new-token workloads.

alex: Good. Next actions: mike runs the two canaries and posts perf artifacts; jin adds metrics; tara drafts a small kernel-selection tweak (prefers fused on fragmented heaps).

jin: thanks — posting canary link when ready. :thumbsup:
